## Overview

This report documents a post hoc semantic stimulus audit of the word stimuli used in the sentence-completion analyses. Six local language models rated each isolated word on blinded semantic items indexing psychological depth, self-reflective relevance, existential meaning, reflective cognition, personal or emotional salience, and reverse-keyed surface-level qualities.

The purpose of the audit is limited. It asks whether the target word sets are rated as semantically deeper than their comparison word sets by local LLM judges. It should be interpreted as post hoc stimulus-level semantic evidence rather than as a claim that isolated-word ratings exhaust the construct.

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(knitr)
  library(readr)
  library(scales)
  library(stringr)
  library(tidyr)
})

report_root <- normalizePath("..", mustWork = TRUE)
path_here <- function(...) file.path(report_root, ...)

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_, formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits))
}

fmt_p <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    NA_character_,
    ifelse(x < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)))
  )
}

fmt_df <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    NA_character_,
    ifelse(abs(x - round(x)) < .001, formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2))
  )
}

pretty_check <- function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(
    x,
    reflective_vs_practical_words = "Reflective vs practical",
    inner_life_vs_object_words = "Inner-life vs object",
    cova_depth_vs_control_words = "Cova depth vs control",
    clean_overall_depth_vs_control_words = "Overall depth vs control",
    abstraction_gradient_ordering = "Abstraction gradient",
    .default = x
  )
}

pretty_item <- function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(
    x,
    y_psychological_depth = "Psychological depth",
    y_self_reflective_relevance = "Self-reflective relevance",
    y_existential_meaning = "Existential meaning",
    y_reflective_cognitive_process = "Reflective cognitive process",
    y_personal_emotional_salience = "Personal/emotional salience",
    y_concrete_observable_depth_keyed = "Concrete/observable, depth-keyed",
    y_logistical_transactional_depth_keyed = "Logistical/transactional, depth-keyed",
    y_impersonal_neutral_depth_keyed = "Impersonal/neutral, depth-keyed",
    .default = x
  )
}

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_family = "Times New Roman", base_size = 12))
```

## Scoring Items

The model prompts were blinded to the experimental group labels. Source metadata were joined back only after scoring. Each model rated each word on 1-10 scales with half-points allowed. Three surface-level items were reverse-keyed before computing the composite.

```{r}
#| label: scoring-items
item_table <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Item, ~Direction, ~Included_in_composite,
  "Psychological depth", "Direct", "Yes",
  "Self-reflective relevance", "Direct", "Yes",
  "Existential meaning", "Direct", "Yes",
  "Reflective cognitive process", "Direct", "Yes",
  "Personal/emotional salience", "Direct", "Yes",
  "Concrete/observable", "Reverse-keyed", "Yes",
  "Logistical/transactional", "Reverse-keyed", "Yes",
  "Impersonal/neutral", "Reverse-keyed", "Yes"
)

knitr::kable(item_table, caption = "Semantic rating items used in the local-model audit.")
```

The composite used below is `psychological_depth_composite`, computed after depth-keying the reverse items.

## Mixed-Effects Validation

The core validation question was whether depth-related words received higher LLM-rated psychological-depth scores than their matched comparison words. Following the mixed-model decision rule used for this project, fixed-effect p values were computed as Type 3 conditional F-tests with Kenward-Roger approximation through `afex` and `pbkrtest`. Estimates, confidence intervals, and slope/contrast degrees of freedom were obtained with `emmeans` using Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.

For each binary contrast, the model was:

```{r}
#| label: binary-model-formula
#| eval: false
fit <- afex::mixed(
  psychological_depth_composite ~ depth_related_factor +
    (1 + depth_related_factor || rating_model) +
    (1 | word),
  data = dat,
  type = 3,
  method = "KR",
  test_intercept = TRUE,
  expand_re = TRUE,
  check_contrasts = FALSE,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    calc.derivs = TRUE,
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e6)
  )
)

anova(fit)

emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
  fit$full_model,
  ~ depth_related_factor,
  lmer.df = "kenward-roger"
)
contrast(emm, "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "control")
```

For the abstraction-gradient analysis, the model was:

```{r}
#| label: gradient-model-formula
#| eval: false
fit <- afex::mixed(
  psychological_depth_composite ~ abstraction_max_level +
    (1 + abstraction_max_level || rating_model) +
    (1 | word),
  data = dat,
  type = 3,
  method = "KR",
  test_intercept = TRUE,
  expand_re = TRUE,
  check_contrasts = FALSE,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    calc.derivs = TRUE,
    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e6)
  )
)

anova(fit)

emmeans::emtrends(
  fit$full_model,
  ~ 1,
  var = "abstraction_max_level",
  lmer.df = "kenward-roger"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: lme4-fixed-effects-table
fixed_effects_table <- fixed_effects |>
  mutate(
    Analysis = pretty_check(check),
    Estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    SE = round(std_error, 3),
    `95% CI` = paste0("[", fmt_num(ci_lower_kr), ", ", fmt_num(ci_upper_kr), "]"),
    `KR F test` = paste0(
      "F(", fmt_df(num_df_kr), ", ", fmt_df(den_df_kr), ") = ",
      fmt_num(f_value_kr, digits = 2)
    ),
    `p value` = fmt_p(p_value_kr),
    `Observations` = n_obs,
    `Words` = n_words,
    `Models` = n_models,
    `Singular fit` = singular
  ) |>
  select(Analysis, Estimate, SE, `95% CI`, `KR F test`, `p value`, Observations, Words, Models, `Singular fit`)

knitr::kable(
  fixed_effects_table,
  caption = "Fixed effects from mixed-effects validation models."
)
```

All focal fixed-effect estimates were positive. The binary contrasts indicate that depth-related words were rated as more psychologically deep than comparison words across the local-model panel. The abstraction-gradient estimate indicates higher composite ratings at higher abstraction levels.

```{r}
#| label: lme4-fixed-effects-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.8
fixed_effects |>
  mutate(
    Analysis = factor(pretty_check(check), levels = rev(pretty_check(check))),
    ci_low = ci_lower_kr,
    ci_high = ci_upper_kr
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = Analysis)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.35, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high), linewidth = 0.55) +
  labs(
    x = "Fixed-effect estimate",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Estimated semantic-depth differences",
    subtitle = "Positive values indicate higher local-LLM depth ratings for depth-related or more abstract words"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: per-model-binary-differences
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
per_model_binary |>
  mutate(
    Analysis = pretty_check(check),
    rating_model = str_replace_all(rating_model, "_", " ")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = difference_depth_minus_control,
    y = reorder(rating_model, difference_depth_minus_control)
  )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.35, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~Analysis, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Mean depth-related minus control difference",
    y = "Local LLM",
    title = "Per-model depth/control differences"
  )
```

## Abstraction Gradient

The abstraction-gradient stimulus set had three ordered levels. The plotted means show the average LLM-rated psychological-depth composite by local model and abstraction level.

```{r}
#| label: abstraction-gradient-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
per_model_abstraction |>
  mutate(rating_model = str_replace_all(rating_model, "_", " ")) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = abstraction_max_level,
    y = psychological_depth_composite,
    color = rating_model,
    group = rating_model
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(per_model_abstraction$abstraction_max_level))) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    x = "Abstraction level",
    y = "Mean psychological-depth composite",
    color = "Local LLM",
    title = "Abstraction-gradient ratings by model"
  )
```

## Reliability

The semantic rating battery showed high internal consistency both at the word-by-model level and after averaging ratings across models for each word.

```{r}
#| label: reliability-overall-table
reliability_overall |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = analysis,
    `Observations` = n_observations,
    `Words` = n_words,
    `Models` = n_models,
    `Cronbach alpha` = round(cronbach_alpha, 3),
    `McDonald omega total` = round(mcdonald_omega_total, 3),
    `McDonald omega hierarchical` = round(mcdonald_omega_hierarchical, 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Overall reliability estimates.")
```

```{r}
#| label: reliability-by-model-table
reliability_by_model |>
  transmute(
    `Local LLM` = rating_model,
    `Words` = n_words,
    `Cronbach alpha` = round(cronbach_alpha, 3),
    `McDonald omega total` = round(mcdonald_omega_total, 3),
    `McDonald omega hierarchical` = round(mcdonald_omega_hierarchical, 3)
  ) |>
  arrange(`Local LLM`) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Reliability estimates by local model.")
```

## Multilevel CFA

Because the 696 rows are not independent observations, the CFA used `word` as the clustering variable. The model decomposed the measurement structure into within-word and between-word components:

```{r}
#| label: multilevel-cfa-formula
#| eval: false
level: 1
  within_depth =~ y_psychological_depth +
    y_self_reflective_relevance +
    y_existential_meaning +
    y_reflective_cognitive_process +
    y_personal_emotional_salience +
    y_concrete_observable_depth_keyed +
    y_logistical_transactional_depth_keyed +
    y_impersonal_neutral_depth_keyed

level: 2
  between_depth =~ y_psychological_depth +
    y_self_reflective_relevance +
    y_existential_meaning +
    y_reflective_cognitive_process +
    y_personal_emotional_salience +
    y_concrete_observable_depth_keyed +
    y_logistical_transactional_depth_keyed +
    y_impersonal_neutral_depth_keyed
```

The full eight-item model was complemented by a direct-item-only sensitivity model using the five direct psychological-depth items.

```{r}
#| label: cfa-fit-table
fit_keep <- c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr", "srmr_within", "srmr_between", "aic", "bic")

cfa_fit_table <- bind_rows(
  cfa_fit_full |> mutate(Model = "Full 8-item model"),
  cfa_fit_direct |> mutate(Model = "Direct 5-item model")
) |>
  filter(measure %in% fit_keep) |>
  mutate(
    Measure = recode(
      measure,
      chisq = "Chi-square",
      df = "df",
      pvalue = "p value",
      cfi = "CFI",
      tli = "TLI",
      rmsea = "RMSEA",
      srmr = "SRMR",
      srmr_within = "SRMR within",
      srmr_between = "SRMR between",
      aic = "AIC",
      bic = "BIC"
    ),
    Value = case_when(
      measure == "chisq" ~ fmt_num(value, digits = 2),
      measure == "df" ~ fmt_df(value),
      measure == "pvalue" ~ fmt_p(value),
      TRUE ~ fmt_num(value, digits = 3)
    )
  ) |>
  select(Model, Measure, Value) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Measure, values_from = Value)

knitr::kable(cfa_fit_table, caption = "Multilevel CFA fit measures.")
```

```{r}
#| label: direct-cfa-loadings-table
cfa_loadings_direct |>
  filter(op == "=~") |>
  transmute(
    Level = lhs,
    Indicator = pretty_item(rhs),
    `Standardized loading` = round(est.std, 3),
    SE = round(se, 3),
    `p value` = scales::pvalue(pvalue)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Direct-item multilevel CFA standardized loadings.")
```

```{r}
#| label: cfa-icc-table
cfa_icc |>
  transmute(
    Indicator = pretty_item(indicator),
    ICC = round(icc, 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Indicator intraclass correlations by word cluster.")
```

The reliability estimates were strong, but the full eight-item single-factor CFA was not uniformly clean. The direct-item-only CFA fit was better, especially for within-cluster SRMR. This pattern is consistent with a coherent depth-oriented semantic battery, while also suggesting that reverse-keyed surface-level items may add method variance.

## Interpretation For Manuscript Use

The most defensible manuscript use is as a post hoc semantic stimulus audit:

> As a post hoc stimulus audit, six local language models rated each target and comparison word on blinded semantic items indexing psychological depth, inwardness, reflection, and abstraction. Mixed-effects models showed that target words were consistently rated as more psychologically deep than comparison words, supporting the intended semantic contrast of the stimulus sets.

This should be described as stimulus-level semantic evidence. It supports the semantic direction of the stimulus manipulation under local LLM judgments.
